blogs.title: How DeepSeekMath Found 120B Math Tokens in the Wild Web
blogs.description: A behind-the-scenes tour of the data pipeline that turned Common Crawl into a high-quality, 120B-token math corpus. We’ll unpack the fastText classifier, iterative domain mining, human-in-the-loop curation, aggressive deduping, and benchmark decontamination—plus why this approach generalizes to other domains like code.

blogs.title: Small Model, Big Brains: Why DeepSeekMath-7B Rivals Giants
blogs.description: An accessible look at how a 7B-parameter model can approach GPT-4 and Gemini-Ultra on math benchmarks. We explain the power of curated data at scale, starting from a code model, and how focused pretraining beats sheer parameter count for structured reasoning tasks.

blogs.title: GRPO, Explained: The Leaner, Meaner RL That Boosts Math Reasoning
blogs.description: PPO without the critic? Meet Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). This post demystifies how GRPO uses group baselines, cuts memory costs, stabilizes updates with KL regularization, and lifts MATH accuracy to 51.7%—all with clear analogies and minimal math.

blogs.title: From Chain-of-Thought to Program-of-Thought: Teaching Models to Show Their Work
blogs.description: How DeepSeekMath blends chain-of-thought, Python-based program-of-thought, and tool-integrated reasoning during instruction tuning. We cover why showing steps matters, when code execution helps, and how these strategies push performance toward 60% on MATH with tools.

blogs.title: Math Beyond English: Why Multilingual Pretraining Pays Off
blogs.description: DeepSeekMath’s corpus wasn’t just English—and that mattered. Learn how multilingual math data drove strong results on Chinese benchmarks (e.g., CMATH), what that implies for global education and research, and how multilingual signals can generalize reasoning.

blogs.title: Benchmarks, Decoded: What GSM8K, MATH, miniF2F, MMLU, and BBH Really Measure
blogs.description: A plain-language guide to the key benchmarks in the paper and what DeepSeekMath achieved on each. We explain grade-school vs. competition math, formal theorem proving with Isabelle, and why math pretraining also lifted general reasoning (MMLU, BBH) and protected coding skills.

blogs.title: The ArXiv Surprise: Why Research Papers Didn’t Move the Needle
blogs.description: Conventional wisdom says arXiv helps math models. This study says: not much—at least for the tested setups. We summarize the experiments, discuss possible reasons (format, domain mismatch, scale), caveats, and what better data curation might look like.

blogs.title: A Unified Map of ‘Alignment’ Methods—and Why RL Actually Helped
blogs.description: SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO—how do they fit together? We outline a simple framework (data source, reward function, algorithm), show why online sampling and graded rewards matter, and explain the key finding: RL improved robustness (better Maj@K), not raw Pass@K capability.
